correctness.rationale: Eliminating both hub coordinates and zero-mean leaf fluctuations by completing squares yields the exact quadratic-form decomposition with Schur M_{a,b}=[[h−2^p/a,z],[z,h−2^p/b]]. Its normalized matrix M/2^p has positive definite derivative for p≥1 (the two eigenvalues y′±w′ are positive), so a unique first loss of negative type occurs between p=1 and p=2; the equality p=2 only at (1,1). On (1,2), 0<z<h; comparing determinant at the zero eigenvalue while fixing a+b proves strict increase with ab, not just numerical monotonicity. Equal-leaf root and its Taylor expansion yield the 1/m correction. The Schur nullity yields centered embedding dimensions. Independently checked full graph distance matrices against the 2×2 elimination in small asymmetric cases and strict ordering for totals 3..17.

final_claim: For unweighted diameter-three double-star tree T_{a,b} with a,b≥1, all-scale Gaussian positivity for distance power p is equivalent to p≤p_{a,b}, where p_{a,b}∈(1,2] is the unique zero of the maximal eigenvalue of a specified explicit 2×2 Schur matrix. For fixed a+b this threshold strictly increases with ab, and the balanced root, asymptotic and critical Euclidean embedding dimensions are exact.
limitations: All-scale Gaussian positivity for unweighted double-star trees, not general trees/weighted variants.
Small direct spectra corroborate but do not replace unique-root and balancing proofs.
